problem: Decide, for each new support ticket, whether to page the on-call engineer now or queue the ticket for the next business day.

fit.reason: Whether a message describes an urgent product failure is a judgment about reading; the customer tier and the incident link are lookups code already has.

decisions.description: Page the on-call engineer now, or queue the ticket for the next business day.

costs.false_positive: An engineer is woken for a ticket that could have waited until morning.
costs.false_negative: A customer with a real outage waits a full business day for a first reply.

subject.description: Ticket subject line as the customer typed it.

body.description: Ticket body text as the customer typed it.

deterministic.description: The sender address belongs to the company's own domain.
deterministic.computed_by: compare the sender domain with the company domain list

deterministic.description: The ticket's account already has an open incident with an owner.
deterministic.computed_by: look the account up in the open-incident table
billing table lookup by account id

questions.instructions: The message asks the company for help with a problem using the product.
questions.purpose: Catches marketing mail, auto-replies and vendor pitches that reach the support inbox and would otherwise be judged as if they were customers.

threshold.why: A real customer request discarded as noise is the costly error, so only a confident no may drop a ticket.

questions.instructions: Which topic best describes what the customer needs from the company?
questions.purpose: Separates outages and security reports, which can page, from billing and how-to questions, which never do.

options.outage: The customer reports that the product is down or unusable for them or their users.
options.security: The customer reports a way that accounts, data or access could be reached by someone who should not reach them.
options.billing: The customer asks about an invoice, a charge, a refund or a plan change.
options.how_to: The customer asks how to do something the product supports.
options.none: None of these describes the message.

threshold.why: An unclear route escalates instead of queueing, which protects the missed-outage error.

questions.instructions: A reasonable on-call engineer would want to be paged about this message right now.
questions.purpose: Holistic baseline: the one-question answer the composed system has to beat.

threshold.why: The baseline is read at its plain yes or no verdict, so both errors count the same.

questions.instructions: How much damage is the problem described in the message doing to the customer right now?
questions.purpose: Ranks how bad an outage report is, so a cosmetic complaint does not page and a total failure does.
criteria: The product works and the customer describes a cosmetic flaw or a minor annoyance.
One feature misbehaves and the customer can still finish their work another way.
An important feature is broken and the customer's work is held up.
The product is unusable for the customer or for all of their users.

threshold.why: A low bar for confidence keeps borderline outage reports in play rather than dropping them.

questions.instructions: The customer states that the problem stops them from finishing their work.
questions.purpose: Adds the customer's own account of impact, which matters most for enterprise accounts.

threshold.why: Impact stated by the customer is a weighted signal, so it should count when the engine is reasonably sure.

questions.instructions: The message reports that customer data has been exposed to a third party.
questions.purpose: Catches a data exposure written up as an ordinary question, which must page whatever else is true.

threshold.why: A missed exposure is the worst error in this system, so a moderately confident yes is enough to page.

page.why: Staff and test tickets never page.
An open incident already has an owner working on it.
Mail that is not a request for help is never a page.
Any sign of exposed data or a security report pages, whatever the other answers say.
An outage report where important work is held up pages.
Enterprise accounts page on a lower combined signal than the single-question rules above.
When the engine cannot say what the message is about, a stronger reader decides instead of a default.

escalation.description: A reasoning model reads the whole ticket and returns page or queue with its reason.

ground_truth.source: on-call acknowledgement outcome recorded by the paging tool: paged and acted on, or paged and dismissed as not urgent

calibration.promotion: Enforce only after every question clears its threshold on at least 100 labelled tickets with balanced accuracy at or above 0.85 and escalation under the declared ceiling.

provenance.notes: Synthetic support-triage system used to test the question-system tools.
